phase_name: Cross-directory double-start and lock-root degradation coverage

objectives.description: Create test-gate-lock-host-scope.sh with two independent fixture roots (serialization, non-vacuousness control, 2 degradation cases, no-leak)
Register suite in suite-classification.data (integration, invokes run-all.sh,task-lock.sh)
Verify: suite passes from neither-fixture-root dir, lint-unit-integration-boundary clean, test-manifest-scripts-sync passes, shellcheck clean

approaches_tried.approach: Tested the 'every tier exhausted' degradation case by pointing the whole battery subprocess's TMPDIR at an unwritable directory
approaches_tried.reason: run-all.sh's own internal mktemp calls (shared fixture build, SUITE_OUT, OUT_DIR) also honor TMPDIR, so this broke run-all.sh's own unrelated plumbing, not just the resolver's tier 4 -- confirmed directly

approaches_tried.approach: Tested 'every tier exhausted' as a direct CLI call against the fixture's deployed task-lock.sh (gate-acquire-host) instead of through the full run-all.sh battery, using the UID-override technique (UID=999999999) to defeat tier 3 (/run/user/$UID) without touching the real path or changing the process's real uid
approaches_tried.reason: isolates exactly what needs proving (resolver returns non-zero with the named ERROR line) without colliding with run-all.sh's own TMPDIR-dependent internals; the override-unwritable case already proves the call site's general fail-open wiring since it does not inspect WHY gate-acquire-host failed

approaches_tried.approach: First attempt at the two degradation cases used --only <fixture suite> to keep the battery fast
approaches_tried.reason: a --only-narrowed run skips the whole gate-lock acquire branch entirely ('specs/.gate-lock is not touched for a narrowed run') by design, so neither degradation case ever reached the acquire branch it meant to exercise -- discovered by direct reproduction outside the suite before fixing
